newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical wins silicone implant ruling.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical wins silicone implant ruling.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Monday a federal appeals court ruling that the company is not liable for injury claims by recipients of Dow Corning temporomandibular joint implants has implications for breast implant claims.

Dow Chemical said the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit in St. Paul, Minn., on Friday upheld a lower court ruling dismissing it from all federal lawsuits involving silicone temporomandibular joint (TMJ) implants.
The implants were once marketed by Dow Corning, a 50-50 joint venture between Dow Chemical and Corning Inc.

Dow Corning also was once the nation's largest maker of silicone-gel breast implants and has been in bankruptcy court for two years trying to deal with claims from thousands of women that the implants caused various illnesses, including lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and connective tissue diseases.

The bankruptcy proceedings have effectively frozen litigation against Dow Corning, so many plaintiffs have filed claims against Dow Chemical because of silicone worker safety testing the company did on behalf of Dow Corning in the 1940s and '50s.
The appeals court ruled that the testing did not constitute legal grounds for holding Dow Chemical directly liable for the plaintiffs' alleged injuries.

Dow Chemical has long maintained that it never tested, made or sold any implants and that it was never notified by Dow Corning that any of the silicone compounds it tested would be used in medical implants.

A U.S. District Court judge in Detroit on Monday is expected to decide whether to allow a breast implant trial against Dow Chemical to proceed in New Orleans. On May 9, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in Cincinnati, Ohio, ruled that all breast implant cases naming Dow Chemical and Corning Inc as defendants be consolidated in Detroit.

Dow Chemical general counsel John Scriven said Friday's TMJ appeals ruling is a "major finding reflecting a maturing legal consensus that there is no basis in the law or the facts for Dow Chemical to be in the silicone litigation."
"The Eighth Circuit ruling is consistent with Dow's dismissal from some 4,000 silicone gel breast implant cases in New York, California and Michigan," Scriven said.
